description: A form within a Notes application renders incorrectly, showing missing fields, overlapping elements, incorrect layout, or fields in the wrong tab or section compared to its intended design.
symptoms: Fields appear missing, out of order, or overlapping on the form
Layout regions, tabs, or subforms do not render as designed
Form displays correctly for some users but not others
Issue appeared after a design change or template update
possible_causes: Local design cache is outdated compared to the server design
Corrupted design element within the form itself
Conflicting subform or shared field referenced by the form is broken
Client display/rendering settings or screen resolution causing layout issues
diagnostic_questions: Does the form display incorrectly for all users or only specific ones?
Was a design change or template update made recently?
Does the issue persist after refreshing the local design?
Are any embedded subforms or shared fields involved in the affected form?

commands.purpose: Refresh the local/server design of the database from its template to correct outdated or corrupted form elements
commands.expected_result: Design refresh completes and the form renders correctly afterward
commands.abnormal_result: Form still displays incorrectly after refresh, indicating a genuine design defect rather than a cache issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm whether the issue affects all users or only specific ones.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps distinguish between a server-side design defect and a local client cache or display issue.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Refresh the local design cache by closing and reopening the database, or running a design refresh.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves cases where the client is using an outdated cached copy of the form design.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open the form in Domino Designer to check for broken subforms, shared fields, or layout regions.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Identifies specific corrupted or misconfigured design elements causing the display issue.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the form on a different workstation or screen resolution.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rules out a local display or resolution-related rendering issue rather than a design defect.

possible_solutions: Refresh the database design from the template
Repair broken subforms or shared fields in Designer
Republish the corrected template and refresh affected databases
Adjust the user's display settings if resolution-related
prevention: Test form changes across multiple resolutions before deployment
Use version control for design changes
Validate subform and shared field references after edits
Schedule regular design refreshes for widely used applications
keywords: fields missing on form lotus notes

description: A view within a Notes application does not update to show new, modified, or deleted documents, displaying outdated data even after documents are known to have changed.
symptoms: Newly created documents do not appear in the view
Deleted documents still appear in the view listing
Modified document values are not reflected in view columns
Manually pressing F9 or Refresh does not resolve the issue
possible_causes: View index has not been rebuilt since the underlying data changed
View is set to manual refresh rather than automatic
Corrupted view index requiring a full rebuild
Replication has not yet delivered the underlying document changes
diagnostic_questions: Does pressing F9 (Refresh) resolve the issue, even temporarily?
Is the view configured for automatic or manual refresh?
Does this affect one specific view, or all views in the database?
Could replication delay explain why changes are not yet visible?

commands.purpose: Force a rebuild of all view indexes in the specified database from the server console
commands.expected_result: View indexes rebuild successfully and the view reflects current data
commands.abnormal_result: View still fails to refresh after rebuild, suggesting index corruption requiring deeper repair

troubleshooting_steps.action: Manually refresh the view using F9 or the Refresh option.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Confirms whether this is a simple refresh timing issue versus a deeper index problem.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the view's properties for its refresh mode, such as manual, automatic, or scheduled.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A view set to manual refresh will not update automatically, which may explain the perceived issue.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run updall -R against the database from the server console to rebuild view indexes.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Rebuilding the index resolves cases where the existing index has become out of sync with the data.

troubleshooting_steps.action: If only one specific view is affected, delete and recreate its index definition in Designer.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Isolated view corruption may require rebuilding that specific view rather than the whole database.

possible_solutions: Change the view's refresh mode to automatic if appropriate
Rebuild view indexes using updall -R
Recreate a specific corrupted view definition
Wait for or force replication if the delay is due to unsynced changes
prevention: Schedule regular view index maintenance for high-traffic databases
Set appropriate refresh modes based on how views are used
Monitor for index corruption after server crashes
Educate users on manual refresh options for views set that way intentionally

description: A view's underlying index becomes corrupted, causing incorrect document counts, missing documents, errors when opening the view, or repeated failures even after refresh attempts.
symptoms: Error message when attempting to open a specific view
View shows an incorrect or clearly wrong document count
Documents known to exist do not appear despite refreshing
View crashes the client or causes it to become unresponsive when opened
possible_causes: Improper server or client shutdown while the view index was being updated
Underlying database corruption affecting the view index structure
A very large or complex view formula causing indexing failures
Disk-level errors affecting the database file containing the index
diagnostic_questions: Does the error occur consistently every time this specific view is opened?
Was there a recent server crash or improper shutdown?
Do other views in the same database work correctly?
Has database maintenance such as compact or fixup been run recently?

commands.purpose: Force a full rebuild of all view indexes to attempt to resolve corruption
commands.expected_result: Indexes rebuild successfully and the view opens and displays correctly
commands.abnormal_result: Rebuild fails or the view remains broken, indicating underlying database corruption requiring Fixup or Compact

commands.purpose: Repair structural corruption in the database that may be affecting the view index
commands.expected_result: Fixup completes and reports the database has been repaired
commands.abnormal_result: Fixup reports unresolved corruption, requiring restoration from backup

troubleshooting_steps.action: Attempt to rebuild the view index using load updall -R against the database.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the standard first step to resolve most view index corruption without deeper database repair.

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the view still fails, run Fixup against the database to check for and repair structural corruption.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Fixup addresses corruption at the database level that a simple index rebuild cannot fix.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Compact on the database after Fixup completes successfully.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Compact reclaims space and can resolve additional issues left after structural repair.

troubleshooting_steps.action: If corruption persists, restore the database from the most recent clean backup.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Severe corruption that Fixup cannot resolve typically requires restoring a known-good copy.

possible_solutions: Rebuild view indexes with updall -R
Run Fixup and Compact on the affected database
Simplify an overly complex view formula if identified as a factor
Restore the database from backup if corruption is unresolved
prevention: Ensure clean server and client shutdowns whenever possible
Schedule regular Fixup and Compact maintenance tasks
Monitor disk health on servers hosting critical databases
Avoid overly complex view selection formulas where simpler alternatives exist

description: An agent within a Notes application fails to execute when triggered manually or automatically, producing an error or simply not performing its intended action.
symptoms: Error message when manually running the agent
Agent's expected output or document changes do not occur
Agent log shows a failure or exception
Agent appears to run but completes with no effect
possible_causes: Agent has insufficient execution rights (signer's access level too low)
Agent code contains a runtime error, such as a null object reference
Agent's signer ID has expired or lacks necessary server access
Server security settings restrict the agent from running (restricted/unrestricted agent list)
diagnostic_questions: Does the agent fail every time, or only under certain conditions?
What does the agent log show when the failure occurs?
Is the agent signed by a user or ID with adequate access rights on the server?
Has the server's agent security list (restricted/unrestricted) been recently modified?

commands.purpose: Display the current agent manager schedule from the server console to confirm the agent is queued to run
commands.expected_result: Agent appears correctly scheduled
commands.abnormal_result: Agent does not appear in the schedule, indicating a scheduling or security configuration issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the agent log for specific error details from the failed run.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The log typically provides the exact line or reason for failure, focusing troubleshooting efforts.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify the agent's signer has sufficient access rights on the server, particularly for restricted operations.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Agents run with the rights of their signer, and insufficient rights are a common cause of silent or explicit failures.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the server's Security document to confirm the signer is on the appropriate restricted or unrestricted agent list.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Server security settings can block agents from running certain operations even with a valid signer.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the agent's code for runtime errors, such as referencing a document field that may not exist.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Code-level bugs are a frequent cause of agents failing partway through execution.

possible_solutions: Re-sign the agent with an ID that has sufficient rights
Add the signer to the appropriate server agent security list
Fix the underlying code error causing the runtime failure
Adjust agent trigger settings if scheduling is the root cause
prevention: Test agents thoroughly in a non-production environment before deployment
Maintain proper signer ID management and renewal schedules
Document required server security settings for critical agents
Review agent logs periodically even when agents appear to be working

description: An agent configured to run on a schedule, such as hourly or daily, does not execute at its expected time, leaving its intended automation unperformed.
symptoms: Agent's scheduled actions never occur at the expected time
Agent log shows no recent execution entries
Agent manager statistics show the agent as disabled or not scheduled
Manually running the agent works fine, but the schedule does not trigger it
possible_causes: Agent Manager task is not running on the server
Agent's schedule setting was disabled or misconfigured
Server's agent execution time window excludes the agent's scheduled time
Database containing the agent is not enabled for scheduled agent execution on this server
diagnostic_questions: Is the Agent Manager (amgr) task currently running on the server?
What schedule is configured for the agent, and does it match expectations?
Are there server-level restrictions on agent execution time windows?
Is the database's server correctly set to allow scheduled agents to run?

commands.purpose: View the current schedule of agents managed by the Agent Manager task
commands.expected_result: The agent appears in the schedule with the expected next run time
commands.abnormal_result: The agent is missing from the schedule, indicating a configuration or Agent Manager issue

commands.purpose: Confirm the Agent Manager (AMgr) task is currently running on the server
commands.expected_result: AMgr is listed as an active task
commands.abnormal_result: AMgr is not listed, meaning no scheduled agents will execute until it is restarted

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the Agent Manager task is running on the server using show tasks.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: No scheduled agents can run at all if the Agent Manager task itself is not active.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the agent's schedule settings in Designer to confirm they match the intended trigger time and frequency.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An incorrectly configured schedule will simply never trigger the agent as expected.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the server document for any agent execution time restrictions that might exclude the scheduled time.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some servers restrict scheduled agent execution to specific windows, which can silently prevent agents from running.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify the database is hosted on a server enabled for running scheduled agents.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some servers are configured to disallow scheduled agent execution entirely for performance or policy reasons.

possible_solutions: Restart the Agent Manager task if it is not running
Correct the agent's schedule configuration
Adjust server-level agent execution time restrictions
Move the database to a server that supports scheduled agent execution
prevention: Monitor Agent Manager task status with automated alerts
Document expected agent schedules for reference during troubleshooting
Review server agent restrictions periodically
Test scheduled agents after any server migration or reconfiguration

description: A button on a form or view in a Notes application does not perform its intended action when clicked, either doing nothing, throwing an error, or performing the wrong action.
symptoms: Clicking the button produces no visible effect
An error message appears when the button is clicked
Button performs an unexpected or outdated action
Button works for some users but not others
possible_causes: Button's underlying formula or script contains an error
User lacks sufficient access rights for the action the button performs
Local design cache is outdated, running an old version of the button code
Button relies on a field, agent, or other design element that has since changed or been removed
diagnostic_questions: Does the button fail for all users or only specific ones?
Is there an error message, and if so, what does it say exactly?
Was the button's code recently modified?
Does the affected user have appropriate ACL access for the intended action?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the button is running its current, intended code
commands.expected_result: Button behavior matches the current design after refresh
commands.abnormal_result: Button still fails after refresh, pointing to a genuine code or access rights issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Note the exact error message, if any, when the button is clicked.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Specific error text often points directly to the failing line of formula or script.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Refresh the local design cache by closing and reopening the database.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves cases where the client is running an outdated cached version of the button's code.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the affected user's ACL access level against what the button's action requires.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Insufficient access rights will cause certain button actions, such as document creation or field updates, to silently fail.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open the button in Designer and review its formula or script for errors or outdated references.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly identifies bugs or broken references to other design elements that may have changed.

possible_solutions: Fix the underlying formula or script error in the button
Adjust the user's ACL access level appropriately
Refresh local design caches for affected users
Update the button to reference current, valid design elements
prevention: Test button actions across different user access levels before deployment
Use version control and testing for design changes
Document required ACL levels for key application actions
Refresh design caches after significant application updates

description: A user attempts to save a document in a Notes application, but the save fails, either silently, with an error message, or by reverting to the previous state after appearing to save.
symptoms: Error message indicating the document could not be saved
Save appears to complete but changes are not actually persisted
Document reverts to its prior state after closing and reopening
Issue occurs consistently for one user or one specific document
possible_causes: User does not have sufficient ACL access (at least Author rights) to save the document
A validation formula on the form is silently blocking the save
The document is locked by another user or process
Insufficient disk space on the server hosting the database
diagnostic_questions: Does the user have at least Author access with Create/Edit rights in the database ACL?
Is there an error message, or does the save simply appear to have no effect?
Could a required field be failing validation without a clear error shown?
Is there sufficient free disk space on the server hosting this database?

commands.command: File > Application > Access Control (Notes client, if administrator)
commands.purpose: Check the user's current access level in the database ACL
commands.expected_result: User has Author access or higher with appropriate create/edit rights
commands.abnormal_result: User has Reader access or lower, explaining why the save is blocked

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the database ACL to confirm the user has sufficient access to create or edit documents.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Insufficient ACL access is one of the most common causes of a document failing to save.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the form for validation formulas that might be silently preventing the save.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A validation formula failing without a clear message can appear as if the save simply is not working.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check whether the document is currently locked by another user or session.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Document locking, if enabled, will prevent saves from other users while the lock is active.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify sufficient free disk space on the server hosting the database.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A server with no free disk space cannot write new or updated documents to the database.

possible_solutions: Adjust the user's ACL access level appropriately
Fix or clarify the validation formula blocking the save
Release the document lock held by another user or session
Free up disk space on the hosting server
prevention: Set ACL access levels appropriately based on user roles
Provide clear error messages for validation formula failures
Monitor server disk space proactively
Educate users on document locking behavior where enabled

description: A user attempts to open or edit a document but is informed it is currently locked by another user, preventing edits even though the other user may no longer actually be working on it.
symptoms: Error message stating the document is locked by another user
User can view but not edit the document
Lock persists even after the other user has closed the document or logged off
Multiple users report being unable to edit the same document over time
possible_causes: Document locking is enabled and another user genuinely has the document open for editing
A stale lock remains after the other user's session crashed or disconnected improperly
Document locking settings are misconfigured, causing locks to persist longer than intended
Replication conflict created an unexpected lock state
diagnostic_questions: Is document locking intentionally enabled for this application?
Is the user who allegedly holds the lock currently active, or did their session end abnormally?
How long has the lock been in place?
Does this happen with one specific document or across many documents in the database?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design in case a locking-related design element needs updating (used alongside manual lock review)
commands.expected_result: No direct effect on locks, but confirms design is current before further troubleshooting
commands.abnormal_result: N/A - this step is primarily precautionary before manual lock investigation

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm whether the user holding the lock is still actively working on the document.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If they are genuinely editing, the lock is functioning as intended and should not be forcibly removed.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check how long the lock has been active and whether the locking user's session ended abnormally.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A stale lock from a crashed session is the most common cause of a lock persisting incorrectly.

troubleshooting_steps.action: As an administrator, manually clear the document lock using administration tools if confirmed stale.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Removing a confirmed stale lock restores normal editing access without waiting for automatic expiration.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the database's document locking configuration if this occurs frequently.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Frequent stale locks may indicate a configuration issue, such as too long a lock timeout setting.

possible_solutions: Wait for the legitimate lock holder to finish and release it
Manually clear a confirmed stale lock as an administrator
Adjust document locking timeout settings if stale locks recur often
Disable document locking for the application if it is not actually needed
prevention: Set reasonable lock timeout values for locking-enabled applications
Encourage users to close documents properly rather than force-closing sessions
Only enable document locking where genuinely necessary
Monitor for recurring stale lock patterns
keywords: document locked by another user notes

description: A computed field on a form shows an incorrect, outdated, or unexpected value rather than the result its formula should logically produce based on current document data.
symptoms: Computed field shows a value that does not match its formula logic
Field value does not update when related fields change
Field shows blank or an error indicator instead of a computed value
Issue appears only on certain documents, not all
possible_causes: Field is set to compute only on document creation rather than recalculate on edit
Formula references a field that has been renamed, removed, or is empty
Local design cache is outdated, using a previous version of the formula
Circular or conflicting formula logic between multiple computed fields
diagnostic_questions: Is the field set to 'Computed', 'Computed for display', or 'Computed when composed'?
Does the formula reference any fields that might be missing or renamed?
Does refreshing the document or design resolve the incorrect value?
Are there other computed fields whose formulas might interact with this one unexpectedly?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the computed field is using its current formula
commands.expected_result: Field displays the correct computed value after refresh
commands.abnormal_result: Field still shows an incorrect value, pointing to a genuine formula logic issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the field's compute type, such as Computed, Computed for display, or Computed when composed.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The compute type determines when the formula runs, and a mismatch with expectations explains many apparent bugs.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the field's formula for references to other fields that may be missing, renamed, or blank.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A formula referencing an invalid or empty field will often produce blank or incorrect results.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Refresh the local design cache and reopen the affected document.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Resolves cases where the client is displaying results based on an outdated cached formula.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test the formula in isolation using Designer's formula debugging tools if available.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps pinpoint exactly where the formula logic diverges from the expected result.

possible_solutions: Change the field's compute type to match the intended behavior
Fix formula references to renamed or missing fields
Refresh design caches for affected users
Resolve conflicting logic between interacting computed fields
prevention: Document field compute types and dependencies during design
Test formulas thoroughly after renaming or removing fields
Use consistent naming conventions to avoid broken references
Review computed field logic when making related design changes

description: A document fails to save because a validation formula on the form determines that required conditions are not met, but the resulting error message is unclear or the condition itself may be incorrectly configured.
symptoms: Error message referencing a validation failure when attempting to save
User cannot identify which field or condition is causing the validation to fail
Validation blocks save even though the document appears correctly filled out
Issue occurs consistently for specific documents or field combinations
possible_causes: Validation formula logic contains an error causing it to fail incorrectly
Required field referenced by the validation formula is blank or improperly formatted
Validation formula was recently changed and is stricter than intended
Hidden or computed fields involved in validation are not populating as expected
diagnostic_questions: What exact validation error message is displayed?
Which field or fields does the validation formula check?
Was the validation formula recently added or modified?
Does the issue occur only with certain data entered, or in all cases?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the form is using its current validation formula
commands.expected_result: Validation behaves as expected after refresh if the issue was cache-related
commands.abnormal_result: Validation still incorrectly blocks the save, indicating a genuine formula logic issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Note the exact validation error message and which field it references.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Pinpoints exactly which condition in the formula is failing, focusing further investigation.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open the form in Designer and review the validation formula logic for the referenced field.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Allows direct inspection of whether the logic itself is correct or overly strict.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test saving the document with different sample data to isolate the exact triggering condition.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Helps confirm whether the validation is working as intended but simply needs correct data, or is genuinely broken.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Correct the validation formula logic if it is found to be inaccurate or overly restrictive.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Directly resolves the issue by aligning the validation with its intended business rule.

possible_solutions: Correct the underlying validation formula logic
Ensure referenced fields are properly populated before save
Improve the validation error message for clarity
Refresh design caches if the issue was due to an outdated formula version
prevention: Write clear, specific error messages for validation formulas
Test validation formulas thoroughly with various data scenarios
Document the business rules behind each validation condition
Review validation logic when related fields are changed

description: The Domino server service or process is not running on the host machine, making all databases, mail routing, and directory services on that server completely unavailable.
symptoms: Users cannot connect to the server at all
Server does not respond to console commands or remote administration
Operating system service manager shows the Domino service as stopped
No server activity visible in logs since the stop occurred
possible_causes: Service was manually stopped for maintenance and not restarted
Server crashed due to an unhandled error or resource exhaustion
Operating system-level issue prevented the service from continuing to run
Scheduled maintenance or patching process stopped the service unexpectedly
diagnostic_questions: Was any planned maintenance or patching scheduled around the time the service stopped?
Does the operating system event log show any errors related to the Domino service?
Can the server be reached at the operating system level, such as via remote desktop or SSH?
Has this happened before, suggesting a recurring stability issue?

commands.purpose: Attempt to manually start the Domino server service on Windows
commands.expected_result: Service starts successfully and the server becomes reachable
commands.abnormal_result: Service fails to start, requiring review of the operating system and Domino logs for the underlying cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm at the operating system level whether the Domino service is stopped or crashed.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Establishes the exact current state before attempting any restart.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review operating system and Domino server logs for errors around the time the service stopped.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Log entries often reveal the specific cause, such as a crash, resource exhaustion, or manual stop.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Attempt to manually start the Domino service.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Determines whether the service can start cleanly now that the immediate cause may have passed.

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the service fails to start, investigate underlying operating system issues such as disk space, memory, or corrupted files.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A failure to start often points to a deeper system-level problem that must be resolved first.

possible_solutions: Manually restart the Domino server service
Resolve underlying operating system issues preventing startup
Free up system resources if exhaustion caused the crash
Escalate to the server or infrastructure team for persistent instability
prevention: Set up service monitoring and automated alerts for the Domino service
Schedule and communicate planned maintenance clearly
Maintain adequate system resources on the server
Configure automatic service restart on failure where appropriate

description: An attempt to start the Domino server fails, with the process terminating shortly after launch or reporting a startup error before reaching a normal operating state.
symptoms: Server process starts and then immediately terminates
Startup error message referencing a specific database, port, or configuration issue
Server console shows startup halting partway through initialization
Service remains in a stopped or failed state after each startup attempt
possible_causes: Corrupted or locked system database, such as names.nsf or log.nsf, preventing startup
Port conflict with another process using the same network port
Server ID file is missing, corrupted, or password-protected without the password available
NOTES.INI misconfiguration introduced by a recent manual edit
diagnostic_questions: What specific error message or log entry appears at the point startup fails?
Was any change made to NOTES.INI or system databases recently?
Is another process potentially using the same network port as Domino?
Is the server ID file present, accessible, and does its password (if any) match what is expected?

commands.purpose: Attempt to repair a corrupted log.nsf that may be preventing server startup
commands.expected_result: Fixup completes and the server can subsequently start normally
commands.abnormal_result: Fixup fails or the server still cannot start, pointing to a different underlying cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review the exact startup error message or console output at the point of failure.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Startup failures typically report a specific reason, which directs the rest of the troubleshooting.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for recent changes to NOTES.INI and review them for errors.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Manual configuration changes are a common and easily overlooked cause of startup failures.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Verify no other process is using the same network ports required by Domino.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Port conflicts will prevent the server from binding and completing startup.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the server ID file is present, valid, and its password is correctly configured if required.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A missing, corrupted, or inaccessible server ID will halt startup very early in the process.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Run Fixup against critical system databases such as log.nsf if corruption is suspected.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Corrupted system databases required during initialization can prevent successful startup.

possible_solutions: Correct NOTES.INI misconfiguration
Resolve port conflicts with other processes
Restore or reconfigure a valid server ID file
Repair corrupted system databases with Fixup
prevention: Back up NOTES.INI before making manual changes
Document and test configuration changes in a non-production environment first
Maintain secure, accessible backups of server ID files
Monitor for port conflicts when deploying new services on the same host

description: The Domino server consistently shows very high CPU utilization, causing slow response times for users and potentially triggering performance alerts, without a clear single cause immediately apparent.
symptoms: Server CPU usage consistently at or near 100%
Users experience slow response times across mail and applications
Specific server tasks show unusually high processing activity
High CPU usage may be constant or occur in recurring spikes
possible_causes: A runaway or inefficient agent consuming excessive CPU
Full-text indexing or a large view rebuild running during peak hours
Excessive replication activity from too many concurrent replicas
A stuck or looping server task consuming CPU without completing
diagnostic_questions: Which specific server task or process is consuming the most CPU?
Does high usage correlate with a specific time of day or recurring scheduled task?
Have any new agents or applications been deployed recently?
Is the high usage constant, or does it spike and then subside?

commands.purpose: List currently running server tasks to identify which one may be consuming excessive CPU
commands.expected_result: Tasks are shown with normal, expected activity levels
commands.abnormal_result: A specific task shows unusually long-running or repeated activity, pointing to the source of high CPU usage

commands.purpose: Display current CPU utilization statistics from the server console
commands.expected_result: CPU usage within normal operating range
commands.abnormal_result: CPU usage consistently very high, confirming the reported performance issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use show tasks to identify which server task is most active during the high CPU period.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Isolates the specific process responsible rather than treating the server as a whole black box.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if high CPU correlates with scheduled agents, indexing, or replication activity.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many high CPU incidents are tied to identifiable scheduled processes rather than random spikes.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review recently deployed agents or applications for inefficient loops or excessive processing.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: New or modified code is a common source of unexpected CPU consumption.

troubleshooting_steps.action: Adjust scheduling of resource-intensive tasks, such as indexing or large agents, to off-peak hours.
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Redistributing load away from peak usage times reduces user-facing impact even if total CPU work is unchanged.

possible_solutions: Fix or disable an inefficient runaway agent
Reschedule resource-intensive tasks to off-peak hours
Reduce unnecessary concurrent replication activity
Add server resources if sustained legitimate load has grown
prevention: Monitor CPU usage trends and set proactive alerts
Review new agents for performance impact before production deployment
Schedule maintenance-heavy tasks during low-usage windows
Periodically review and optimize high-traffic applications
